content.text: I've read the brief against the release. Here's my check.

facts.evidence: Reported net revenue was $57.3 billion, up 28%; managed net revenue (non-GAAP) was $58.0 billion, up 27%, or up 15% excluding significant items (non-GAAP).
JPMorganChase reported second-quarter 2026 net income of $21.2 billion ($7.70 per diluted share) ... Net income was $21.2 billion, up 41%, and diluted EPS was $7.70, up 47%.
The Firm states net income excluding significant items (non-GAAP) of $16.9 billion, or $6.14 per share, up 13%.

facts.note: The brief gives the Equity Markets ($6.0B, +86%) and Fixed Income Markets ($6.1B, +6%) components, but never states total Markets revenue of $12.1 billion, up 35%, predominantly driven by Equity Markets.

facts.evidence: ROE was 24%; ROTCE (non-GAAP) was 29%, or 23% excluding significant items (non-GAAP).

facts.note: Firmwide net interest income of $25.6 billion, up 10%, is not stated; the brief mentions only Corporate NII (down $667 million).

facts.evidence: The significant items were a $4.6 billion net gain related to Visa shares (Corporate) and $1.0 billion of gains on certain equity investments ($763 million Corporate, $263 million CIB).
Distributions: $4.0 billion common dividend ($1.50 per share) and $6.2 billion of net common repurchases; net payout ratio of 73% for the last twelve months.
CET1 capital of $303 billion; estimated Standardized ratio 14.1%, Advanced 14.2%
Credit costs were $2.5 billion, with $2.4 billion of net charge-offs (down $44 million) and a $149 million net reserve build, primarily in Wholesale, versus a $439 million build a year ago.

claims.claim: Second-quarter 2026 net income was $21.2 billion, or $7.70 per diluted share.
Reported revenue was $57.3 billion.
Significant items totaled $5.6 billion, consisting of a Visa-related net gain and equity investment gains.
claims.note: The $5.6 billion total is an unshown sum of the $4.6B Visa gain and $1.0B equity investment gains; the release quantifies the significant items' effect as a $4.2 billion (after-tax) reduction to net income and never presents a $5.6 billion aggregate.

claims.claim: Reported net revenue was $57.3 billion, up 28% year over year.
Managed net revenue (non-GAAP) was $58.0 billion, up 27% year over year.
Managed net revenue was up 15% excluding significant items (non-GAAP).
Net income was $21.2 billion, up 41% year over year.
Diluted EPS was $7.70, up 47% year over year.
Net income excluding significant items (non-GAAP) was $16.9 billion, or $6.14 per share, up 13%.
The significant items were a $4.6 billion net gain related to Visa shares in Corporate.
The significant items included $1.0 billion of gains on certain equity investments, of which $763 million was in Corporate and $263 million in CIB.
Return on common equity was 24%.
ROTCE (non-GAAP) was 29%, or 23% excluding significant items.
Noninterest expense was $27.3 billion, up 15%, driven by higher compensation, brokerage, marketing, technology and occupancy expense.
Reported overhead ratio was 48% and managed overhead ratio (non-GAAP) was 47%.
Credit costs were $2.5 billion, with $2.4 billion of net charge-offs, down $44 million.
There was a $149 million net reserve build, primarily in Wholesale, versus a $439 million build a year ago.
CIB net revenue was $24.9 billion, up 27%.
CIB net income was $9.7 billion, up 46%.
CIB ROE was 22%.
Investment Banking fees were $3.3 billion, up 30%.
Equity Markets revenue was $6.0 billion, up 86%.
Fixed Income Markets revenue was $6.1 billion, up 6%.
CCB net revenue was $20.3 billion, up 8%.
CCB net income was $5.3 billion, up 3%.
CCB ROE was 34%.
Card Services & Auto revenue rose 12%.
CCB noninterest expense rose 13%.
Card Services net charge-off rate was 3.34%.
AWM net revenue was $6.9 billion, up 19%.
AWM net income was $2.0 billion, up 33%.
AWM ROE was 48%.
AUM was $5.1 trillion, up 18%.
AWM client assets were $7.7 trillion, up 19%.
Corporate net revenue was $6.0 billion, up $4.5 billion, but down $805 million excluding significant items (non-GAAP).
Corporate net income was down $1.5 billion excluding significant items, partly reflecting the absence of a prior-year $774 million income tax benefit.
The release provides no financial guidance or outlook for future periods.
Dimon said market sentiment remains constructive for continued investment banking activity.
Dimon cited geopolitical tensions, sticky inflation, large global fiscal deficits and elevated asset prices as risks.
CET1 capital was $303 billion.
The estimated Basel III Standardized CET1 ratio was 14.1% and the Advanced ratio 14.2%.
The Firm's supplementary leverage ratio was 5.5%.
Estimated total loss-absorbing capacity was $590 billion on estimated Standardized RWA of $2.1 trillion.
The Firm paid a common dividend of $4.0 billion, or $1.50 per share, and made $6.2 billion of common stock net repurchases.
Net payout ratio was 73% over the last twelve months.
Book value per share was $133.01, up 9% year over year.
Tangible book value per share (non-GAAP) was $113.35, up 10% year over year.
Total assets were $5.0 trillion at June 30, 2026.
Equity Markets revenue rose 86% on strong performance across products and regions.
Dimon attributed the results to a particularly favorable environment.
Noninterest expense grew 15% while revenue excluding significant items grew 15%.
Expense drivers include front-office headcount growth and revenue-related compensation.
CCB net charge-offs rose $70 million, predominantly Card Services, with reserves flat.
Corporate net interest income fell $667 million on lower rates.
